key_insight: Four-tetrahedron macro-element condensation shrinks interior-point Newton systems, enabling faster and more memory-efficient equilibrium-based plasticity solves on CPUs and GPUs.
engineering_relevance: The approach makes larger 3D elastoplasticity and limit-analysis computations feasible while retaining statically admissible stress fields.
method: Eliminate stress directions and macro-internal traction-continuity multipliers to obtain reduced systems compatible with positive-definite factorizations.
Establish nonsingularity conditions, using trace-bound augmentation for von Mises limit analysis.
Use CUDA Fortran batched macro-local operations and cuDSS sparse solves, with a memory-saving PCG option for elastoplasticity.
evidence_signal: Reported tests show up to 2× CPU speedup and 66.5% lower peak linear-solver memory versus stress-only elimination, plus GPU speedups up to 13.5× over the CPU counterpart and 87.5× over MOSEK.
watch_item: The reported gains are benchmark-dependent, and the lower-memory GPU PCG option increases solution time relative to the direct GPU solver.
paper_title: A GPU Interior-Point Solver with Macro-Element Condensation for Equilibrium-Based Plasticity
